quiz.q: With the def2 basis sets, how are palladium's inner (core) electrons described?
options: By an effective core potential (ECP) that replaces 28 core electrons
quiz.explain: For elements beyond Kr, the def2 basis sets come with an ECP that replaces the core and includes scalar-relativistic effects. Q-Chem needs ECP = def2-ECP.

quiz.q: This reaction breaks the bond between Pd and a large π ligand. Which effect from earlier experiments is likely to matter a lot?
quiz.explain: Large, polarizable ligands bound to a metal have substantial dispersion contributions. Uncorrected functionals typically underbind.

quiz.q: Your job is killed at the 10-minute limit. The most sensible next step is…
options: Use a smaller basis or a cheaper setting, and say in your report how this limits the accuracy
quiz.explain: Every real calculation is a compromise between accuracy and cost. State the compromise you made and its likely consequences: that's part of a good report.

predictions.prompt: Before you compute: what bond dissociation energy do you expect for your method?
Will your method land within chemical accuracy (±1 kcal/mol) of the reference?
predictions.note: Check the result card in “Explore your data”.

questions.text: Write your report (**about 300 words**): title, the method you chose and why (with references), the complete computational setup, your result compared with the reference value of 16.20 kcal/mol, and a short conclusion.
If you had ten times more computer time, what would you change in your calculation, and why?
